title: [Bug] ttnn.expm1_bw returns a zero gradient for x <= -6.25 (bf16) / -17 (fp32): the derivative is built as expm1(x) + 1
body:
### Describe the bug

`ttnn.expm1_bw` returns a gradient of exactly `0` for every input below `-6.25` in bfloat16 and `-17` in float32, although `d/dx expm1(x) = exp(x)` is an ordinary normal float all the way down to `x = -87.34`, where it is still `1.2e-37`.

The composite builds the derivative out of the forward result instead of calling `exp`
([`unary_backward.cpp#L1334-L1343`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary_backward/unary_backward.cpp#L1334-L1343)):

```cpp
// bw(expm1) = grad * expm1(input) + 1
std::vector<Tensor> expm1_bw(
    const Tensor& grad, const Tensor& input, const std::optional<MemoryConfig>& output_mem_config) {
    std::vector<Tensor> grad_tensor;
    Tensor eresult = ttnn::expm1(input, output_mem_config);
    Tensor rp1 = ttnn::add(eresult, 1.0f, std::nullopt, output_mem_config);
    Tensor result = ttnn::multiply(grad, rp1, std::nullopt, output_mem_config);
    grad_tensor.emplace_back(result);
    return grad_tensor;
}
```

`expm1(x) + 1` equals `exp(x)` in exact arithmetic only. `expm1(x)` tends to `-1` from above and rounds to **exactly** `-1` as soon as `exp(x)` falls below half an ULP of `1` — below `2^-9` for bfloat16 and `2^-25` for float32. The `+ 1` then cancels completely and the entire gradient is lost. This is the cancellation `expm1` exists to avoid, reintroduced in the one place where plain `exp` was what was wanted.

### Repro

```python
import torch, ttnn

device = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0)
x = torch.tensor([[-5.0, -10.0, -17.0, -20.0, -30.0, -60.0, -85.0]], dtype=torch.float32)
t = ttnn.from_torch(x, dtype=ttnn.float32, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT, device=device)
g = ttnn.from_torch(torch.ones_like(x), dtype=ttnn.float32, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT, device=device)

print(ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.expm1_bw(g, t)[0]))
# tensor([[6.7379e-03, 4.5419e-05, 0., 0., 0., 0., 0.]])
print(torch.exp(x.double()))
# tensor([[6.7379e-03, 4.5400e-05, 4.1399e-08, 2.0612e-09, 9.3576e-14, 8.7565e-27, 1.2161e-37]])
```

### Observed vs expected

float32, gradient `1`, golden `exp(x)` in float64. ULP is the integer distance between float32 bit patterns:

| input | got | want | ULP |
|---|---|---|---|
| -5 | 0.006737947 | 0.006737947 | 1 |
| -10 | 4.541874e-05 | 4.539993e-05 | 5,170 |
| -17 | **0** | 4.139938e-08 | 858,902,297 |
| -20 | **0** | 2.061154e-09 | 822,977,587 |
| -30 | **0** | 9.357623e-14 | 701,675,270 |
| -60 | **0** | 8.756511e-27 | 338,522,313 |
| -85 | **0** | 1.216099e-37 | 36,013,792 |

bfloat16, gradient `1`, ULP between bfloat16 bit patterns:

| input | got | want | ULP |
|---|---|---|---|
| -3 | 0.05078125 | 0.04980469 | 4 |
| -4 | 0.01953125 | 0.01831055 | 10 |
| -6.25 | **0** | 0.001930237 | 15,101 |
| -6.28125 | **0** | 0.001869202 | 15,093 |
| -10 | **0** | 4.529953e-05 | 14,398 |
| -40 | **0** | 4.255494e-18 | 8,861 |
| -85 | **0** | 1.219575e-37 | 550 |

The relative error over the zeroed band is 100%. The rows above the threshold show the same cancellation in a milder form: at `x = -10` in float32 the gradient is already 5,170 ULP off.

### Affected input range

All 65,536 bfloat16 bit patterns as the input, gradient `1`, counting inputs whose exact gradient is a normal float but whose result is exactly zero (subnormal inputs and gradients outside the float32 normal range excluded):

| dtype | zeros where the golden is normal | affected range | max ULP | mean ULP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bfloat16 | 487 | `[-87, -6.25]` | 15,101 | 105.29 |
| float32 | 295 | `[-87, -17]` | 858,902,297 | 3,266,830 |

### Which architectures

All of them. `expm1_bw` is a host-side composite in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary_backward/unary_backward.cpp`, so Wormhole and Blackhole build the same op graph and produce the same values.

### How it was verified

ttsim Blackhole v1.10.6 (`TT_METAL_SIMULATOR=libttsim_bh.so`, slow dispatch). Exhaustive sweep of all 65,536 bfloat16 bit patterns as the input with an all-ones gradient, in both bfloat16 and float32, against `exp(x)` evaluated in float64. Subnormal inputs (flushed by the hardware) and gradients outside the float32 normal range are excluded.

`test_backward_expm1.py::test_bw_expm1` does not catch it: it draws inputs from `[-10, 10]` and asserts PCC only, which the large positive values dominate.

![expm1_bw before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/badnikhil/tt-metal/pr-assets/tt-metal-expm1-bw.png)
